title: Alerts backend: rules, evaluation job, queue/summary/badge endpoints
objective: All eleven alert types are materialized by a reconciliation job driven by tenant thresholds, exposed via summary/queue/badge endpoints with per-user new-since-last-visit semantics, and re-evaluated after workflow operations (spec FR-61..FR-63, A-6, §9.4).
scope: IAlertRule implementations for the 11 types incl. ExecutiveEscalationRule (Q-10)
AlertEvaluationJob (15 min) + targeted re-evaluation via IAlertReevaluationQueue
Alert clearing/downgrade when the triggering condition resolves
out_of_scope: Dashboard attention panels (T-032/T-033 consume these endpoints)
implementation_details: Liquibase 130-alerts: alerts (tenant_id, id, type text check in ('unassigned_lead','overdue_follow_up','stalled_lead','stalled_quote','quote_expiring','quote_expired','sla_breach','high_value_stalled','pending_pricing_approval','awaiting_underwriting','executive_escalation'), lead_id, quote_id null, severity text, premium_at_risk numeric null, created_at, resolved_at null, resolved_reason text null, unique open alert per (tenant_id,type,lead_id,coalesce(quote_id,0)) via partial index); user_alert_views (user_id, tenant_id, last_opened_at, PK(user_id,tenant_id))

Domain/Alerts/IAlertRule.cs: interface { AlertType Type; IReadOnlyList<AlertCandidate> Evaluate(AlertEvaluationContext ctx); } with pure implementations per type parameterized by TenantSettings — one class per rule under Domain/Alerts/Rules/ (UnassignedLeadRule: lead status new + age > unassigned_lead_hours; OverdueFollowUpRule; StalledLeadRule (open pre-quote, no activity stalled_lead_days); StalledQuoteRule; QuoteExpiringRule (valid_until within quote_expiry_alert_days); QuoteExpiredRule; SlaBreachRule (assignment/underwriting/received-to-sent targets); HighValueStalledRule; PendingPricingApprovalRule (pending > pricing_approval_target_days); AwaitingUnderwritingRule; ExecutiveEscalationRule per Q-10: highValue && (stalled || overdue || expiring) || strategicParty && stalled); AlertEvaluationContext carries prefetched lead/quote snapshots so rules stay pure and unit-testable

Infrastructure/Jobs/AlertEvaluationJob.cs (recurring */15 min): per tenant, compute candidates, reconcile with open alert rows: insert missing (created_at now), resolve rows whose condition cleared (resolved_reason 'rule_cleared'); workflow operations that touch an item enqueue targeted re-evaluation (Hangfire fire-and-forget) implementing IAlertReevaluationQueue from T-019 — completing an action thereby clears or downgrades its alert (FR-62 Action column semantics)

Features/Alerts: GetAlertSummaryQuery -> category cards {type, definition, count} + rollup {premiumAtRisk, quoteCount}; ListAlertsQuery {tab: all|escalated|overdue|expiring|sla, ownerUserId, productLineId, coverTypeId, regionId, priority, paged} joining lead/quote display fields (ref, client, broker or 'Direct', premium at risk, stage chip data, age, owner, flags); GetBadgeQuery -> count of alerts created after user_alert_views.last_opened_at (0 when no row); ResetBadgeCommand upserts last_opened_at=now

Tab mapping: escalated -> executive_escalation + high_value_stalled; overdue -> overdue_follow_up; expiring -> quote_expiring + quote_expired; sla -> sla_breach + awaiting_underwriting + pending_pricing_approval

findings.description: The GET /alerts 'ownerUserId' filter matches a lead where the user holds ANY lead assignment role, while the row's displayed owner (OwnerUserId/OwnerName) is resolved from the accountable-owner assignment only. Filtering by a user who is, e.g., the underwriter but not the accountable owner returns rows whose owner column shows a different person, so the filter and the displayed 'owner' can disagree.
findings.evidence: AlertStore.ListAsync (src/api/QuoteIQ.Infrastructure/Alerts/AlertStore.cs:204-209) filters on LeadAssignments.Any(a => a.LeadId == x.lead.Id && a.UserId == ownerUserId) with no IsAccountableOwner predicate, whereas GetAccountableOwnersAsync (lines 296-307) joins BusinessAssignments.IsAccountableOwner to populate the owner column.
findings.suggested_fix: Constrain the ownerUserId filter to the accountable-owner assignment (join BusinessAssignments and require IsAccountableOwner) so the filter and the displayed owner use the same 'owner' definition.

findings.description: The alert type 'unassigned_lead' is materialized/resolved correctly and appears in the 'all' queue tab and feeds the badge/rollup, but it is not represented on any of the five summary category cards nor mapped to any queue tab. As a result the sum of the five category-card counts can be less than the 'all' tab total (unassigned alerts are uncarded). This follows PRD 18.2's literal five-card list (Escalated/Stalled/Overdue/Expiring/SLA), so it is likely by-design, but flagged for the T-037 Alerts Center UI to resolve deliberately rather than surface an unexplained count gap.
findings.evidence: AlertDefinitions.Categories (src/api/QuoteIQ.Application/Features/Alerts/AlertDefinitions.cs:39-46) omits AlertType.UnassignedLead from all five cards and TypesForTab (lines 29-36) omits it from every tab; ListAsync 'all' (no type filter) still returns it.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm with the PRD/human whether unassigned_lead should live under the SLA Breaches card (assignment SLA) or its own card; if intentionally uncarded, document it so T-037 does not present a card-sum vs all-tab discrepancy as a bug.
